hero.title: Journey Timeline pattern
hero.description: A vertical timeline of real, dated stages (rescued, foster, today) for a single dog's own detail page — the page a success-story card's storyHref links out to.

rescued.label: Rescued
rescued.description: Found at an overcrowded shelter as the longest resident with no adoption applications. We named her Juniper, because every great journey begins with one opportunity.
rescued.imageAlt: A volunteer greeting the dog on the day of rescue

cleanBillOfHealth.label: Clean Bill of Health
cleanBillOfHealth.description: A wellness exam confirmed she's healthy and ready for the next step — finding her family.

today.label: Today
today.description: Settling into foster care and looking for the right forever home.
today.imageAlt: The dog relaxing at home today

example.title: A dog's own page
example.description: A short intro with name, status and summary, then the story so far as a timeline, then a call to help. The dog's card on the success stories list links here.

example.name: Juniper
example.summary: Juniper was the shelter's longest resident with no adoption applications — now healthy, safe, and looking for her family.
example.ctaTitle: Want to help write the next chapter?

standard.title: Usage rules

stagesType.after: — plain, site-owned array. No built-in sort/filter and no fixed stage vocabulary; labels are free text (e.g. "Rescued", "In Foster Care", "Today").

optionalFields.mid1: is optional — a stage without a
optionalFields.mid2: just omits the date line, and a stage without
optionalFields.mid3: renders text only. Early stages of a real story often don't have media yet.

videoSrc.after: instead of an image — for a real rescue-day video served from the site's media host (`mediaUrl()`). Prefer this over a third-party embed, which can be blocked on posts using licensed (non-original) audio.

partnerLinks.after: credits outside organizations named in the stage's own text (description is plain text, so it can't carry inline links). Always opens in a new tab.

relatedLinks.before: links out to the story behind the stage — the news post or blog entry that announced it. An href starting with
relatedLinks.mid: renders as a client-side link; anything else opens in a new tab. Never use
relatedLinks.after: for an internal route — it always opens a new tab, so the site would open itself in a second one.

pairsWith.mid: that component's curated grid is the "wall," this is the detail page each card's
pairsWith.after: points to — see the composed example above.

standard.rescueJourneys: Composing a full rescue-journeys page (teaser → list → detail): the list/teaser pages are built from `SuccessStoriesSection` (see that pattern's page for the live status-split and auto-rotating-teaser examples); each dog's own detail page renders this component.
